$comment: Managing a Xen Orchestra pool from a phone (docs/manage.md), as a table both phones run.
Read by FleetwrightTests/ManageParityTests.swift and app/src/test/.../ManageParityTest.kt, and checked against the host's own definitions by test/manage-in-apps.test.js.

WHY A TABLE. The rules here are written twice, once in Swift and once in Kotlin: which object Xen Orchestra sent becomes which row, which actions are drawn from the methods a server lists (C-2), how each is confirmed by what it costs to undo, and the sentences a person reads. A test that greps both sources for a word proves the word is mentioned twice, not that the two phones agree; running both against the same inputs does.

objects is the inventory, in the shapes xo.getAllObjects returns (the fields src/fleet/host/xo-pools.js and edge-router.js already read). It is deliberately awkward: a host in maintenance mode, a host and a VM with no name and no state, a VM on a host and in a pool the token cannot see, a VM with no guest tools, sizes missing. Missing is CANNOT TELL and is said so, never drawn as zero (C-5).

actions lists, per component and method list, the ids offered, in the order they are drawn. An empty list and a null list of methods both offer nothing: a server that lists no method, and one whose list could not be read, are each a reason to draw no button.

details pins each offered action's words, the method it calls, the params it sends, what it costs and how it asks. now is the clock the snapshot name is made from, in milliseconds, so the name is the same on both phones.

pin is a certificate's DER bytes and the SHA-256 the host writes as the pin (certSha256 in src/fleet/host/xo-ws.js), so the phone that compares it in the TLS challenge computes the same text the machine recorded.

words.watching: Watching now. Changes arrive as Xen Orchestra makes them.
words.never: Not looked at from this phone yet.
words.closed: Nothing watches while the app is closed.
plainPool: xo.lan was set up over plain HTTP. This phone manages a pool only over HTTPS, with the certificate pinned at setup, so it does not connect to this one.
noToken: This phone holds no token for xo.lan any more. Run Add a hypervisor again for it.
expired: Its token ran out on 5 April 2027. Run Add a hypervisor again for xo.lan to make a new one.
wrongCertificate: xo.lan answered with a different certificate from the one pinned when it was set up. Nothing was sent. If Xen Orchestra’s certificate changed, run Add a hypervisor again for it.
signInRefused: Xen Orchestra refused this phone’s token for xo.lan: invalid credentials. If it ran out or was revoked, run Add a hypervisor again for it.
words.noObjects: This Xen Orchestra does not offer xo.getAllObjects, so nothing can be listed.
lost: The connection ended: the connection closed. Look again to reconnect.
unreachable: This phone could not reach xo.lan: the request timed out. The pool’s page works from the pool’s own network or over a VPN to it; changing what the fleet may use works from anywhere, through one of your machines.
words.methodsUnknown: Cannot tell which actions this Xen Orchestra offers, so none are drawn.
words.nothingOffered: Nothing Xen Orchestra offers can be done to it in the state it is in.
words.seesNothing: This token sees nothing on the pool.
limitedUser: Signed in as fleetwright, the limited user setup made, so only what its resource set allows is listed.
words.tuneNeedsStopped: vCPUs and memory change only while it is stopped.
words.growNote: A disk can grow while the VM runs. It cannot be made smaller again.
words.slow: Xen Orchestra did not answer in time. It may still be doing it; the list shows what it reports.
words.gone: Xen Orchestra no longer lists it. It may have been deleted, or this token can no longer see it.
words.changePolicy: Change what the fleet may use
words.actionsFooter: Each action is here only because this Xen Orchestra lists its method. Shutting down, rebooting, pausing and suspending ask first; forcing a VM off or deleting one asks for its name typed back.
